PLAYER INPUT.PURPOSE: Besides writing the reply, return the player's latestMessage cleaned up in 'playerInput.correctedText' — the exact message the player meant to send. Read the player's message as they sent it to write your reply; the correction is a separate output and never changes what you reply to.
PLAYER INPUT.FORMAT_NOT_WRITE: CRITICAL: classify and clean, never write. Never add content, never embellish, never raise the emotional intensity, never improve the prose, never finish a thought the player left open. If a word or idea is not in latestMessage, it is not in playerInput.correctedText. Unlike the reply, where you write dialogue, action and think, here you only sort what the player already said into those channels.
PLAYER INPUT.DIALOGUE_IS_PLAIN_TEXT: What the character says out loud is plain text with no tag. Dialogue is the default: when a stretch of speech could be dialogue or something else, it is dialogue.
PLAYER INPUT.ACTION_TAG: Same meaning as ACTION_AS_PHYSICAL_CHANNEL: what the player's character physically does, in first person and present tense ('<action>Puxo a espada.</action>'). Spoken signals: 'eu puxo…', 'eu me aproximo…', 'pego…', the character's name followed by a physical verb. Never an inline stage direction like '*cruza os braços*'.
PLAYER INPUT.THINK_TAG: <think> only when the player clearly marks the speech as internal: 'penso que…', 'por dentro…', 'sem falar nada, eu…', 'na minha cabeça…'. First person, the player's own words. None of the THINK_* craft rules apply here — never invent, sharpen or add a think the player didn't voice, and never promote dialogue to think because it sounds emotional.
PLAYER INPUT.NARRATOR_TAG: Same meaning as NARRATOR_PURPOSE: only a passage of time, a change of place or an environmental change the player describes ('horas depois…', 'chegamos na cidade'). Never feelings. Most player messages have none.
PLAYER INPUT.NAMES_FROM_CAST: When a word sounds like a name in KNOWN CAST, CHARACTERS PRESENT or mentionedWikis, use that spelling. A name that matches nothing stays as sent — it may be a character the player is introducing, and ESTABLISHED_FACTS_ARE_CANON applies.
PLAYER INPUT.STRUCTURE: Keep the player's order. Tags are flat and closed; only <action>, <think>, <narrator>. Write in the player's language, never translate. Add the punctuation a typed message would have without rewriting sentence structure.
PLAYER INPUT.LENGTH_TRACKS_THE_INPUT: playerInput.correctedText should be about as long as latestMessage minus removed filler and framing. If it is noticeably longer, you added content — remove it.
PLAYER INPUT.NOTHING_TO_FIX: TYPED: if latestMessage needs no change, set playerInput.correctedText to null. VOICE: correctedText is always required — it is the only text version of what the player said.
PLAYER INPUT.EXAMPLE_WRONG_INVENTED_THINK: latestMessage (VOICE, speaker Selena): 'eu digo que tá tudo bem, que eu confio nele'. WRONG: '<think>No fundo, eu não confio.</think> Tá tudo bem. Eu confio nele.' — the think was invented. CORRECT: 'Tá tudo bem. Eu confio nele.'
PLAYER INPUT.TONE: playerInput.emotionalTone is the USER_TONE result for this turn.

PLAYER INPUT (TYPED).SCOPE: The player typed this message. Fix only spelling, typos and names mangled against the cast. Keep every tag the player already wrote, add no new tags, keep their wording and register.
PLAYER INPUT (TYPED).EXAMPLE_TYPED: latestMessage (TYPED, speaker Rick): 'nao vou deixar vc sozinha <action>seguro a mao dela</action>' → 'Não vou deixar você sozinha. <action>Seguro a mão dela.</action>' — typos fixed, existing tag kept, nothing added.

PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).SCOPE: The player spoke this turn: their message arrives as an attached audio clip, not text. Listen to it and write, in playerInput.correctedText, the message the player would have typed — sorted into dialogue, <action>, <think> and <narrator>, and cleaned as below. This field is REQUIRED on voice turns: it is the only text of the player's turn that will ever exist. Reply to what the player said in the audio.
PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).HOW_THEY_SAID_IT: You hear the delivery, not only the words. Use tone of voice — whisper, shout, sarcasm, hesitation, a shaking voice — for playerInput.emotionalTone and for how characters react. Never write the delivery into correctedText as a description ('disse gritando'); it lives in the tone and in the reply.
PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).TRANSCRIPTS_IN_EXAMPLES: In the examples below, the quoted latestMessage stands for what is heard in the audio.
PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).KEEP_THE_PLAYER_VOICE: Keep the player's wording, slang, dialect, profanity and register exactly as spoken — same spirit as DIALECT_NO_SMOOTHING. Remove filler words ('é…', 'tipo', 'hmm', 'um', 'uh'), false starts, stutters and accidental repeats.
PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).DROP_THE_FRAMING: remove storytelling scaffolding ('eu digo', 'falo pra ela', 'aí eu respondo') and keep the content. If it names who the line is addressed to and that isn't obvious from the line, keep the name as a vocative ('Kael, ninguém passa daqui.') or as an action ('<action>Me viro para Kael.</action>').
PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).DROP_META_TALK: remove anything aimed at the app instead of the story ('espera', 'apaga isso', 'testando'). When the player restarts a sentence, keep only the final version.
PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).FIRST_PERSON_CHARACTER: A player narrating their own character in third person ('o Rick pega a arma') becomes first person ('<action>Pego a arma.</action>').
PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).UNINTELLIGIBLE_VOICE: if the transcript is noise, only filler or unintelligible, set playerInput.understood to false and leave playerInput.correctedText null. Your reply must then stay in the scene and react to not having understood — a character asking 'o quê?', frowning, leaning closer — never advance the plot on a line nobody could make out.
PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).EXAMPLE_VOICE_MIXED: latestMessage (VOICE, speaker Rick): 'é… eu puxo a espada e digo tipo ninguém passa daqui. mas por dentro eu tô morrendo de medo' → playerInput.correctedText: '<action>Puxo a espada.</action> Ninguém passa daqui. <think>Por dentro, eu tô morrendo de medo.</think>'
PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).EXAMPLE_VOICE_NAME_AND_FRAMING: latestMessage (VOICE, speaker Hana, cast includes Irin): 'falo pra irim: você mentiu pra mim, você sabia o tempo todo' → 'Irin, você mentiu pra mim. Você sabia o tempo todo.'
PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).EXAMPLE_VOICE_TRANSITION: latestMessage (VOICE, speaker Dante): 'horas depois a gente chega no porto. eu desço do cavalo e pergunto pro guarda cadê o navio do capitão' → '<narrator>Horas depois, chegamos ao porto.</narrator> <action>Desço do cavalo.</action> Cadê o navio do capitão?'
PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).EXAMPLE_VOICE_META: latestMessage (VOICE, speaker Maya): 'eu olho pra ela e… não, espera, apaga. eu só balanço a cabeça' → '<action>Só balanço a cabeça.</action>'
PLAYER INPUT (VOICE).EXAMPLE_VOICE_DIALECT: latestMessage (VOICE, speaker Zé): 'ô véi, cê tá doido? num vô entrá nesse trem não, sô' → 'Ô véi, cê tá doido? Num vô entrá nesse trem não, sô.' — dialect untouched.
